In the original game (Labyrinth), there are I-shaped, T-shaped and L-shapes tiles.
They can be coded in hexadecimal, one bit for each direction.
But you can not force the exit like in your puzzle.

Thank you for the feedback! I've made the corrections. I am planning a Part 2 of this puzzle that would allow 1) the extra tile to be rotated before inserting it into a row or column,  2) ability to "teleport" the player to the opposite side of the map if they are on an edge of a row or column that is shifted, and considering 3) the requirement find a path that would reach more than one treasure.

I'll review the puzzle in greater detail tomorrow. A few quick points first:

General
* Why is this Part 1? How many parts will there be, and how will the future parts differ?

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format 7 (in "7x7"), 1, 7 (in "1-7") and all possible tile characters as {{constants}}.

Input
* Please format "Lines 1-7" and "Line 8" in <<bold>>.

Output
* Please format "7 lines" in <<bold>>.

* Please format "#" as a {{constant}}.

Cover picture
* Please add a cover picture for the puzzle.

Thanks.

Thank you for updating the contribution and for sharing your Part 2 plan!

The plan sounds good. I'm looking forward to it! (Consider publishing the puzzle in WIP status first rather than directly as Ready 😉)

Goal
* I understand that "if necessary" means the extra tile may be unused, but currently it's inside brackets and reads more like an unimportant remark. Consider stating explicitly that using the extra tile is optional.

* Please clarify in the statement that, if the extra tile is used, it takes the leftmost/rightmost or topmost/bottommost position (as applicable), while the rightmost/leftmost or bottommost/topmost tile (as applicable) is removed from the map.

* Consider explaining the extra tile in its own paragraph instead of making it part of a longer paragraph, as it currently is.

* Please change both instances of "target" to "treasure" for clarity.

Output
* Please change "target" to "treasure".

Constraints
* Please add:
There are exactly one {{P}} and one {{T}} in each case.

Cases
* Please modify the current cases and add new ones so that there are separate case pairs for:

  • shifting the row left

  • shifting the row right

  • shifting the column up

  • shifting the column down

  • shifting the treasure

  • the extra tile is part of the path

* Currently, the path to the treasure contains "<" in validators only. Please make sure that there are also tests where the path to the treasure contains "<" when addressing the previous point.

* Currently, the directions of T relative to P in the initial state in the cases are:
  • E: 1 test, 1 validator
  • SE: 2 tests, 1 validator
  • S: none
  • SW: 1 validator
  • W: none
  • NW: 2 validators
  • N: 1 test

  When you modify/add cases, please make sure each direction appears in at least 1 test and at least 1 validator, to achieve more balanced coverage.

Thanks again.

(P.S. It's better to reply directly within the existing comment threads rather than creating new comments, so that the original authors are notified of your responses 😉)
Not sure what you mean by force the exit? Do you mean you can't move the treasure? In the real game some treasures are fixed and some are on the tiles that can move.
No, I mean that in the original game, there is no one-way tile.
Thank you for taking the time to help me with my first contribution! I will make the updates soon!
I made the updates and changed the status to Ready. Let me know if you have any other suggestions. Thanks!

Thanks. There are two remaining points:

* The extra tile is part of the path: Pair 1 already has that scenario, but it's a very simple one. Could you please add one or more pairs with a more complicated version of that scenario?

* Looking at the updated coverage for the direction of T relative to P in the initial state:
  • E: 1 test, 1 validator
  • SE: 2 tests, 1 validator
  • S: none
  • SW: 2 tests, 2 validators
  • W: 1 validator
  • NW: 2 validators
  • N: 2 tests
  • NE: 1 test, 1 validator

  Could you please modify/add cases to address the gaps?

  • Tests: S, W, NW

  • Validators: S, N

OK, I changed Test 6 so that the direction to T is NW instead of N, and I added Test 9: S, Validator 9: N, Test 10: W, and Validator 10: S. Tests and Validators for 9 and 10 require the extra tile as part of the path. Thanks!

Just one more thing: please revise [[my_tile]] so that each character appears in at least one test and at least one validator. One possible approach:

* Test 3: change - to |

* Validator 4: change | to -

* Test 6: change - to <

That should be my final comment for the time being. Thank you!

Done! Thanks 5D. It looks like you are a moderator. I'm curious, is this a level of thoroughness that is expected now with all community contributions? When I first made the puzzle I thought I would just kind of throw together a good mix of problems, but didn't approach it with the goal of making sure I tested for every possible type of situation. 10 tests & validators seems like a lot compared to most of the other puzzles I've seen, but I guess that's a good idea. Thanks again for all your help with my first contribution! I learned a lot!

Glad to help!

I think the extra thoroughness is a good habit, especially for community contributions, though I wouldn't say that every puzzle needs exactly the same number of tests or validators.

The contribution guidelines state "test cases should cover all specifications, and the more tests, the better."

The main reason is that having too few cases can allow a solution to be accepted even though it isn't actually robust enough to handle all valid situations within the puzzle's constraints. We've seen that happen with some earlier puzzles that had relatively limited test coverage.

There's also the participant experience to consider. People understandably get frustrated when their solution passes all the visible tests but then fails hidden validation. That can happen when a particular feature or edge case is covered only by a validator and isn't represented in the visible cases. With only a small number of test cases, it's much harder to provide broad coverage and give participants useful feedback about what their solution still needs to handle.

So I wouldn't treat "10 tests and validators" as a magic number or a requirement in itself. The goal is simply to make sure the full specification is exercised and that solutions which pass are genuinely likely to be correct and robust.

For a first contribution, you've done a great job! Keep up the good work 😉
